title: Uważam, że…
note:
B2-SPINE Block 8 unit 2 — a SITUATIONS unit in the chunk lane, reusing situation_chunk as every *_func pack does (no new structure ID). It recombines b1_opinions, b2_ze_clauses and the conjunctions, and the recombination is most of the unit's value: the learner already owns moim zdaniem, zgadzam sie, nie zgadzam sie, masz racje, moze and na pewno, and what he has never had is the layer that sits between agreeing and disagreeing.

THE SPINE'S CANDIDATE LIST WAS CUT BY ONE, AND THIS IS THE LOUDEST JUDGMENT CALL IN THE BATCH. The spine offers `wydaje mi sie` ('it seems to me'). check_new.py reports WYDAJE AS ALREADY TAUGHT — by b2_verb_family2 at path 170, FIVE NODES BACK, where it is the third person of wydawac, TO SPEND MONEY. That is the AGENTS homograph trap in its textbook form: mi and sie are owned too, so the whole phrase would be assembled from three strings the learner owns, every one of them meaning something else, and the collision is at the worst possible distance — recent enough to be live in his memory. It was DROPPED rather than taught around, on the standing rule that an uncertain fork takes the conservative path and gets flagged. If James wants it, it needs its own moment naming the collision out loud (the dziekuje / ktorej chunk-to-slot treatment), not a line in a chunk board. `chyba` was brought in to fill the hedging hole it leaves, and is logged as a substitution rather than a silent addition.

SIX NEW WORDS, ORGANISED BY JOB rather than as a vocabulary list, because six near-synonymous adverbs dumped together is precisely the cliff load-splitting forbids: STATING A VIEW (uwazam ze, wedlug mnie) · HEDGING (chyba, raczej) · AGREEING SHARPLY (wlasnie) · REFUSING TO COMMIT (to zalezy). Four jobs, six words, and every slide is one job.

DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, all verified NEW and available: pewnie, naprawde, dokladnie. They are good words and they are near-synonyms of what is already here; adding them would have made the unit a pile of interchangeable adverbs instead of four contrasting jobs. Logged as available for C1 rather than silently skipped.

TAUGHT CHUNKS ARE NEVER DECOMPOSED, and this shaped the quiz more than anything else. b1_opinions owns `mam racje` / `masz racje` and `zgadzam sie` WHOLE; racja, racje and zgadzam are all verified NEW as bare forms. So no item anywhere blanks inside one of those chunks — several otherwise natural quiz items (Masz ___ , Nie ___ sie) were drafted and cut for exactly this reason. The chunks appear only entire.

WEDLUG IS TAUGHT IN ONE FROZEN PHRASE ONLY. It governs the Genitive, and taty and lekarza are both verified NEW — so wedlug taty is unbuildable and absent. `wedlug mnie` works because mnie is genuinely syncretic for ja (the same string in the Genitive and the Accusative, the honest exception AGENTS names for masculine animates), and it is named in one line rather than left to slip past. No other complement of wedlug appears.

UWAZAM IS FIRST PERSON ONLY, on the standing pattern: b2_indirect_q's note records the wiem quarantine ('wiem stays first-person only'), and the same discipline applies here. uwazasz and uwaza are absent. The consequence is stated rather than hidden — Dad can say what HE considers, and asks the other person with material he already owns (Dlaczego tak myslisz? Zgadzasz sie?), which is why those two are on the board.

NIE MIEC RACJI IS FENCED and this is not a fresh decision: B2-SPINE's leaves-to-C1 item 12 books `nie miec racji` and the soft -cja Genitive class explicitly. Nothing in this pack negates racja; disagreement is done with the owned `nie zgadzam sie`.

SYNONYM PAIRS FORCED THE QUIZ DESIGN. uwazam/mysle and wedlug mnie/moim zdaniem are genuine everyday synonyms, so any item offering both as choices would have had two right answers. Every choice list was built so that no item contains a true rival of its own answer, and the English gloss picks out the specific word rather than the general sense. The sharpest item in the stage is the pair that runs the other way: chyba (probably, uncertain) against the OWNED na pewno (certainly), which discriminates the new hedge against a marker he has had since B1.

PISANIE IS EIGHT ITEMS. Twelve is the fixed size of the MATCH board, not of this stage (b1_stories_func ships three), and eight distinct answers produce all six new words plus the two frozen replies. Seven are full_word — single adverbs, or two-word frozen chunks well inside the hard cap — and one is a cloze, because Uwazam, ze kawa jest dobra is a COMPOSED sentence and may not be typed whole at any length. No answer repeats.

intro.title: You can agree and disagree. This is everything in between.
intro.body:
You already own the two ends of a discussion:

Zgadzam się. — I agree.
Nie zgadzam się. — I don't agree.
Moim zdaniem… — In my view…
Masz rację. — You're right.

What you have never had is the middle. Real discussion is mostly not agreeing or disagreeing outright — it is saying something is probably true, or rather not, or that it depends, or that yes, that is exactly the point.

This unit adds six words, and they sort into four jobs. Take them a job at a time rather than as a list; several of them would look interchangeable in a list and are not.

Stating a view — uważam, według
Hedging — chyba, raczej
Agreeing sharply — właśnie
Refusing to commit — zależy
intro.body_pl: Cztery zadania: opinia · niepewność · zgoda · brak decyzji.

intro.title: Stating a view: uważam, że… and według mnie
intro.body:
uważam — I consider, I hold, it is my view. It takes że and then a whole sentence, exactly as myślę and wiem do — that joint is one you have already built.

Uważam, że kawa jest dobra. — I think the coffee is good.
Uważam, że to jest dobra decyzja. — I think this is a good decision.

uważam is a shade firmer than myślę: myślę is what is going through your head, uważam is the position you are taking. Both are ordinary and both are used constantly.

według — according to. You get it in one fixed phrase:

według mnie — in my view, the way I see it

Według mnie ten film jest dobry.

That mnie is the same word you met as the object in boli mnie. Polish uses one shape here for more than one job — the two are genuinely the same string, not two words that happen to look alike. według wants other words in that slot too, and those forms are not taught yet, so według mnie is the whole of it for now.

One limit worth knowing: this unit gives you uważam and no other person of the verb. To ask the other side, use what you already have — Dlaczego tak myślisz? or Zgadzasz się?
intro.body_pl: uważam + że. według mnie — zwrot stały.

examples.en: I think the coffee is good.
In my view this film is good.
examples.pl: Według mnie ten film jest dobry.

intro.title: Hedging: chyba and raczej
intro.body:
Two ways of not fully committing, and they are not the same.

chyba — probably, I think. You believe it, you are not certain.
raczej — rather. It softens what comes next, and it is most often used to take the edge off a no.

Chyba tak. — Probably yes.
Chyba nie. — Probably not.
Raczej nie. — Rather not. / I'd say not.

Set these against a word you have owned since B1:

Na pewno. — Certainly. No doubt about it.

That is the scale: na pewno at one end, chyba in the middle, and raczej nie doing the polite work of declining without a flat refusal. Raczej nie is much softer than nie, and in a discussion it is often the honest answer.
intro.body_pl: na pewno → chyba → raczej nie → nie.

intro.title: Agreeing sharply, and refusing to commit
intro.body:
Two one-word replies that do a great deal of work.

właśnie — exactly; that is just it. It is the reply you give when somebody has said the thing you were about to say. Stronger than zgadzam się, and much more natural in conversation.

— Kawa jest dobra.
— Właśnie!

zależy — it depends. Almost always with to in front:

To zależy. — It depends.

This is the reply that refuses the question as put, and it is entirely polite. Polish uses it exactly where English does.

— Czy to jest dobre?
— To zależy.

What it depends ON needs a form you have not been given, so To zależy stands on its own here — which is, in fairness, how it is most often said anyway.
intro.body_pl: Właśnie — mocna zgoda. To zależy — brak decyzji.

examples.en: — Is the shop open? — It depends.
examples.pl: — Czy sklep jest otwarty? — To zależy.

intro.title: Putting a discussion together
intro.body:
Nothing new on this slide. It is the joins you already have, doing the work they were taught for.

Nie zgadzam się, ale może masz rację. — I don't agree, but maybe you're right.
Chyba tak, ale nie jestem pewny. — Probably yes, but I'm not sure.
Uważam, że to jest dobre, bo kawa jest dobra. — I think it's good, because the coffee is good.

The useful habit here is conceding before you object: masz rację and może cost you nothing and change the temperature of a disagreement completely. Both were yours before this unit.

And to keep a discussion going, ask:

Dlaczego tak myślisz? — Why do you think so?
intro.body_pl: ale · bo · więc — spójniki już znane.

examples.en: I don't agree, but maybe you're right.
examples.pl: Nie zgadzam się, ale może masz rację.

examples.en: Probably yes, but I'm not sure.
examples.pl: Chyba tak, ale nie jestem pewny.

quiz.prompt: ___ tak. (probably yes — you believe it but are not certain)
quiz.explain: chyba is the hedge: you think so, you would not bet on it.

quiz.prompt: ___ tak. (certainly yes — you have no doubt at all)
quiz.explain: The word you have owned since B1, and the far end of the scale from chyba.

quiz.prompt: ___ nie. (rather not — a soft no rather than a flat one)
quiz.explain: raczej takes the edge off the nie that follows it. On its own, nie is blunt.

quiz.prompt: — Kawa jest dobra. — ___! (exactly — that is just what I was going to say)
quiz.explain: Stronger agreement than zgadzam się, and far more natural as a one-word reply.

quiz.prompt: — Czy sklep jest otwarty? — To ___. (it depends)
quiz.explain: The reply that declines the question as it was put — and a perfectly polite one.

quiz.prompt: ___, że to jest dobra decyzja. (I consider, I hold —)
quiz.explain: uważam takes że and a whole sentence after it, exactly as myślę does.

quiz.prompt: Uważam, ___ to jest dobre. (that — joining the sentence on)
quiz.explain: The same joint you built for myślę, że and wiem, że. uważam behaves no differently.

quiz.prompt: ___ mnie ten film jest dobry. (according to me)
quiz.explain: według mnie is a fixed phrase — this unit gives it to you whole and with no other word in that slot.
ale is the real contrast. a would just set two facts side by side without pushing back.

quiz.prompt: ___ masz rację. (maybe you're right — conceding the point)
quiz.explain: może and masz rację were both yours before this unit. Conceding first costs nothing and changes the temperature of a disagreement.

quiz.prompt: Dlaczego tak ___? (do you think — asking the other person to explain)
quiz.explain: You are asking one other person, so the ty form. This unit gives you uważam only in the I form, so this is how you turn the question round.
The one question that keeps a discussion moving after somebody has refused to commit.
